==Problem==
Suppose <imath>a</imath> and <imath>b</imath> are real numbers. When the polynomial <imath>x^3+x^2+ax+b</imath> is divided by <imath>x-1</imath>, the remainder is <imath>4</imath>. When the polynomial is divided by <imath>x-2</imath>, the remainder is <imath>6</imath>. What is <imath>b-a</imath>?
<imath>\textbf{(A) } 14 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 15 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 16 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 17 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 18</imath>

==Video Solution== 
https://youtu.be/l1RY_C20Q2M

==Solution 1==

Use synthetic division to find that the remainder of <imath>x^{3}+x^{2}+ax+b</imath> is <imath>a+b+2</imath> when divided by <imath>x-1</imath> and <imath>2a+b+12</imath> when divided by <imath>x-2</imath>. Now, we solve

<cmath>
\begin{cases}
a+b+2=4 \\
2a+b+12 = 6 \\
\end{cases}</cmath>

This ends up being <imath>a=-8</imath>, <imath>b=10</imath>, so <imath>b-a=10-(-8)=\fbox{\textbf{(E)} 18}</imath>

==Solution 2==
Via the remainder theorem, we can plug <imath>1</imath> in for the factor <imath>x-1</imath> and get <imath>4</imath>, so we have that
<cmath>1^3+1^2+1a+b=4</cmath>
<cmath>a+b=2.</cmath>
Then, we plug in <imath>2</imath> and get a remainder of <imath>6</imath>, so we have that
<cmath>2^3+2^2+2a+b=6</cmath>
<cmath>8+4+2a+b=6</cmath>
<cmath>2a+b=-6</cmath>
Then, we solve the system of equations.
By substitution, we obtain
<cmath>b=2-a</cmath>
<cmath>2a+2-a=-6</cmath>
<cmath>a=-8</cmath>
<cmath>b=2-(-8)=2+8=10.</cmath>
Thus, we have that <imath>b-a=10-(-8)=10+8=\fbox{\textbf{(E)} 18}</imath>

~ranu540

==Solution 3 (Small)==

Using Remainder theorem, we get that:
<imath>4 = (1)^3 + (1)^2 + (1)a + b = 1 + 1 + a + b</imath> so we get  <imath>2 = a + b</imath> (i) and from the second statement,
<imath>6 = (2)^3 + (2)^2 + (2)a + b = 8 + 4 + 2a + b</imath> so we get <imath>-6 = 2a + b</imath> (ii).

So we Subtract (ii) from (i) to get <imath>a = -8</imath>. Substitute in to get <imath>b = 10</imath>.

So <imath>b - a = 10 - (-8) = \fbox{\textbf{(E)} 18}</imath>

~Aarav22

==Solution 4 (Clear Concept)==
When the polynomial <imath>f(x)=x^3+x^2+ax+b</imath> is divided by <imath>x-1</imath>, the remainder is
 <imath>f(1)= 1+1 + a+ b =4</imath> , 
         <imath>a + b =2</imath>

When the polynomial is divided by <imath>x-2</imath>, the remainder is <imath>6</imath>
     <imath>f(2)= 8 + 4 + 2a+ b=6</imath> , 
         <imath>2a + b = -6</imath>
Solving ,  <imath>a + b = 2</imath> and <imath>2a + b = -6</imath> we get <imath>a = -8</imath> , <imath>b = 10</imath> ,
hence , <imath>b-a=18</imath> <imath>\fbox{\textbf{(E)} 18}</imath>

~KENJAKURA
